ideas.risks: May fail because the needed gap-preservation condition could be false for standard residual-based filters; proving a polynomial lower bound on mass may require assumptions absent from the target oracle model.
ideas.summary: Define a concrete residual-forcing filter family (e.g., adaptive rejection based on empirical residual sign + clipping) and prove a theorem: after each round t, every accepted distribution D_t satisfies explicit OPT_C(D_t) ≤ 1/2 - γ_t with γ_t ≥ 1/poly(n,1/ε), and acceptance mass(D_t) ≥ 1/poly(n,1/ε). If proved, instantiate a standard agnostic-boosting framework to obtain ε-accuracy from fixed β.
ideas.title: Prove a polynomially stable filter-gap invariant
ideas.why_promising: This directly isolates the only blocked step in prior attempts and would turn the current conditional route into a complete theorem under a clearly stated wrapper family.

ideas.risks: Existing lower-bound machinery may not separate the exact oracle model; reduction might end up proving only that some restricted boosters fail, not that ε-boosting is impossible.
ideas.summary: Build a fully specified counterexample triplet (class C, distribution D, adaptive filter family F) where OPT_C(D) is small but every adaptive filtering strategy in F can drive OPT_C(D_t) to 1/2 on high-probability rounds while preserving no polynomial mass collapse constraint violation. This would formally refute the unqualified positive route.
ideas.title: Formal filter-instability witness against adaptive residual-forcing
ideas.why_promising: A complete explicit witness would settle the core obstruction claim from Iterations 1–2 and justify why fixed-slack cannot be naively amplified.

ideas.risks: SQ/lower-bound translation may be delicate because the fixed-slack learner outputs hypotheses, not tolerance-calibrated expectation queries, so matching oracle strength may produce only weak negative evidence.
ideas.summary: Formalize the fixed additive oracle as a precision-limited statistical oracle: each call only certifies corr ≥ γ(β) on current distribution, then prove that arbitrary-ε refinement requires query precision Ω(ε) unavailable without additional interface/assumption. Derive impossibility or complexity blow-up under a standard SQ hardness benchmark.
ideas.title: SQ precision barrier for fixed-slack fixed-β amplification
ideas.why_promising: This aligns with the repeated 'precision mismatch' suspicion and could give a principled negative result without relying on class-specific complexity assumptions.

ideas.risks: This may show only that one proof family does not apply cleanly unless it ends at a stronger assumption than the target model permits.
ideas.summary: Complete a theorem-by-theorem normalization table for KMV/Feldman/potential-based agnostic boosting variants in the exact form err ≤ OPT+β for binary predictions, documenting exactly what assumptions they require (advantage definition, margin signals, weighted distribution access) and final excess/complexity dependence.
ideas.title: Precise parameter-convention audit of existing agnostic boosting theorems
ideas.why_promising: The prior notes already suggest this is likely the cleanest path to either a rigorous positive theorem with extra assumptions or a formal statement that current attempts overclaimed applicability.

ideas.risks: Assumption set (e.g., Massart or margin noise) may be too narrow or already known; could produce a high-confidence but weakly useful partial theorem.
ideas.summary: Target classes with low-noise structure (e.g., Tsybakov/Massart noise on bounded-complexity classes, or finite VC + calibration properties) and prove that fixed-β weak learners imply full strong agnostic learners with explicit dependence on noise/margin constants.
ideas.title: Conditional positive theorem under stable-noise / margin hypotheses
ideas.why_promising: It preserves the possibility of a non-vacuous result while honestly separating unconditional and assumption-based progress.

ideas.risks: May only reduce the gap by constants unless one shows a true ε-dependent stage; could risk re-deriving known O(β+ε) results.
ideas.summary: Investigate a two-stage wrapper: use fixed-slack oracle to build a coarse hypothesis and synthetic hard-core residual distribution where ε-dependent structure is amplified via re-sampling/sketching; then apply a second-stage learner tailored to the synthetic residual where the effective target class has bounded excess gap.
ideas.title: Hybrid coarse-to-fine residual reduction
ideas.why_promising: Could bypass full OPT preservation on original D by engineering a new residual domain where fixed slack still yields shrinking effective error across rounds.
